note: Drift pins for every scraper in this repository. tools/check_scraper_pins.py fails the build when a stored artifact violates a pin, when a pinned constant has disappeared from the source, or when a pin has been relaxed without an entry in history. A pin is a promise about a page; changing it is a reviewable event.

pins.why_these: A partial parse of the league-wide report cannot legitimately fall under 100 rows or 10 club tables; a fall of more than 25% against the previous capture is a parse loss, not a report change. The thresholds were chosen from the observed 347-row capture, not fitted to a failure.

history.change: initial pin recorded from the 347-row capture 20261115T121648Z

pins.why_these: The collector downloads pinned nflverse release files and records their sha256; the file hash IS the pin. A changed file changes the hash, which is published in data/model/provenance.json, so it is detected by construction and needs no row pin.

history.change: recorded as hash-pinned rather than row-pinned

pins.why_these: This scraper is superseded by pipeline/capture_snapshots.py, which pins rows, tables, vocabulary and hashes. It is listed here so that nobody mistakes its absence from the pin list for coverage.

coverage_statement: Two scrapers reach the network: pipeline/collect.py (pinned by file hash) and pipeline/capture_snapshots.py (pinned by row count, table count, vocabulary and raw hash). pipeline/scrape_injuries.py is retained but superseded. No other file in the repository performs a network fetch at build time.
